messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@optimo.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — observed nightly idle on committed GPUs

Hey Marcus,

We ran a quick utilization check ahead of the renewal and noticed a recurring pattern: over the last 30 days, ~38-45% of our committed GPU fleet sits below 20% utilization between 0200-0800 PT. That gap is substantial and is driving internal questions on whether the current committed footprint is the right fit for our growth curve.

Options we've discussed internally: shift some of the commit into burst/credits, shorten the committed tranche you quoted, or move to a more flexible autoscale window. Before we start negotiating numbers, can you share any playbooks you have for converting committed capacity into a hybrid model without impacting our peak SLA?

We'd like to avoid a heavy penalty at renewal if usage trends down. Happy to set up a quick call this week. CCing Lauren who is leading ops on our side.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of ML Infrastructure
Optimo AI

--
Attachments: none in this message
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex@optimo.ai>, Lauren Zhou <lauren@optimo.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — observed nightly idle on committed GPUs

Alex / Lauren,

Thanks for the heads-up and the utilization signal — this is exactly the kind of visibility that lets us avoid overcommitting. We have a pragmatic three-part approach we use for customers in this situation:

1) Redistribution matrix: move a tranche of the committed pool (typically 20-30%) into a burst-reserve pool that is priced as a blended credit. This keeps your effective peak capacity intact while reducing steady-state unit cost.

2) Autoscale windows: configure autoscale to allow aggressive scale-down in low-util windows (0200-0800 PT) and rapid scale-up for ML training/peak inference tasks.

3) Timeboxed pilot: 30-60 day pilot to validate that SLOs and tail latencies are preserved. During the pilot we keep the same SLA and provide extra observability (token-level cost + latency heatmaps) so you can watch impact in real time.

I've attached a first-pass redistribution matrix and the July utilization snapshot so you can review the math. Proposal highlights: convert 25% of committed GPUs to burst credits; provide a one-time 10% credit against next invoice if measured monthly utilization across the commit drops >20% compared to last quarter (protects you from overpaying).

If that sounds reasonable we can:
- Lock in a pilot start date (propose Aug 10)
- Share a short mutual action plan link so Legal & Procurement have visibility
- Schedule a 30-minute ops alignment call to pin autoscale windows and observability dashboard panels

Open to tailoring the numbers — if you'd prefer a smaller tranche to start we can do 15% and run a 30-day pilot.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redistribution-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), utilization-snapshot-July.csv (csv)
From: Lauren Zhou <lauren@optimo.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex@optimo.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T08:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal — observed nightly idle on committed GPUs

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — we'll take a pass on the matrix today. A few quick questions before we loop Procurement:

- Can you enumerate the SLA behavior for the burst pool vs committed GPUs? Specifically: 99.9% latency on inference and 1-hour recovery for large training-scale spin-ups?
- The one-time credit you mentioned: is that applied automatically based on our monthly telemetry, or does it require a retroactive claim & approval?
- Pricing delta: what's the blended $/GPU-hour on the 25% burst scenario versus staying 100% committed? We need a baseline to run through forecast models.

If those answers check out we're inclined to accept the 30-day pilot window. Can your team provision a pilot MOP (mutual action plan) for legal + ops to sign off?

Thanks,
Lauren Zhou
VP Engineering, Ops
Optimo AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Optimo pilot pricing/credit recommendation (CONFIDENTIAL)

Soojin / Karthik,

Recap: Optimo sent utilization that shows ~40% low-util windows. They're open to a pilot to validate a ~25% tranche conversion to burst credits. They asked about SLA, pricing delta, and whether the credit is automatic.

My recommendation (to move the renewal forward with minimal churn):
- Offer a 30-day pilot starting Aug 10 that converts 25% of their committed fleet to a burst pool; keep identical SLAs for the pilot period (we can absorb marginal cost risk).
- Pricing: blended $/GPU-hour on burst tranche = committed rate * 1.15 (reflects operational elasticity). That keeps optics simple and still reduces Optimo's steady-state bill.
- Credit: provide a one-time 10% credit applied automatically to their next invoice if measured monthly utilization across the original commit is >20% below their Q2 baseline. This is automatic — no claims process.
- Ops: we'll pre-provision autoscale windows and enable the token-level cost dashboard. Engineering should set a 1-hour warm start for training spin-ups (we can discuss exact buffer).

Risks: short pilot could create churn if they interpret the blended rate as a long-term move. Recommend a clause in the MOP clarifying pilot intent and that permanent commit amendments require separate PO.

If you're good with the above I will:
- Upload the MOP draft to the deal record and send to Optimo for signature
- Subscribe them to a dedicated pilot Slack channel and add Soojin to the ops runbook

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
